lit-narr-01-c3.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Plato's Aesthetics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
lit-narr-01-c3.quote: Poetic narration can take place through narration alone, through mimêsis alone, or by combining the two (392d).
lit-narr-01-c3.claim: The distinction goes back to Plato (Republic, Book 3).

lit-narr-05-c1.text: Dan Shen (2013). Unreliability. the living handbook of narratology (University of Hamburg).
lit-narr-05-c1.quote: reliable when he speaks for or acts in accordance with the norms of the work (which is to say the implied author's norms), unreliable when he does not
lit-narr-05-c1.claim: Booth's working definition: a narrator is unreliable when their account diverges from the work's implied norms.
